decisions.rationale: Residual proposition PASS. The official source explicitly distinguishes IFR from VFR and states the airport-area ATC exception for VFR. Neither 計器飛行方式 nor 有視界飛行方式 is answer-defining in the 365-question canonical inventory. The correct option is uniquely supported and the item does not reuse an existing proposition.

Residual proposition PASS. The source explicitly lists cases in which manned aircraft may fly at or below 150 m outside ordinary takeoff/landing continuation, including search/rescue, doctor helicopters, approved low-level operations and sparsely inhabited or broad-water areas. Q120 only uses doctor-helicopter traffic as one route-planning factor and Q216 tests a UAS no-start action when an aircraft is seen; neither makes the sub-150 m manned-aircraft cases answer-defining.

Residual proposition PASS under the new owner rule, not under the former Tier-B allowance. Q051/Q216/Q218 test concrete UAS avoidance behavior, but the canonical inventory does not make the explicit aircraft-over-UAS right-of-way concept or its source-defined rationale answer-defining. The source states that aircraft navigation safety is prioritized, aircraft have difficulty visually detecting/avoiding small UAS, and UAS generally have higher maneuverability; therefore aircraft are treated as having right-of-way over UAS.

Residual proposition PASS. The source explicitly defines an air traffic control area as designated airspace at or above 200 m above ground/water and requires IFR aircraft in it to remain in communication with ATC and follow instructions. 航空交通管制区 is not answer-defining in canonical inventory.

Residual proposition PASS. The source explicitly defines the air traffic control zone around airports with frequent takeoffs/landings and requires all aircraft, regardless of IFR/VFR, to communicate with ATC and follow flight-method and takeoff/landing-order instructions. 航空交通管制圏 is not answer-defining in canonical inventory.

Residual proposition PASS. The source explicitly distinguishes the three basic restriction surfaces used at all airports: approach surface for final approach/takeoff safety, horizontal surface for low-altitude circling around the airport, and transitional surface for lateral flight such as a go-around. None of 進入表面, 水平表面 or 転移表面 is answer-defining in canonical inventory. The mapping task is central operational airspace knowledge and has one uniquely supported option.
